about.title: Who I am
paragraphs: I'm Naseer — a Software Developer based in Hyderabad, India, currently working full-time at Purple Mavens. I specialise in Angular and the MEAN stack, having shipped 100+ pixel-perfect production UIs, architected a 30+ component library that cut development time by 60%, and delivered complete modules solo from requirements to deployment.

I care deeply about clean architecture, scalable state management with NgRx, and real-time data visualisation. Outside of shipping features, I enjoy mentoring junior developers, driving code quality through reviews, and exploring new tools. I hold a Master's in Computer Science from the University of Kashmir.

blogs.pageSubtitle: Deep dives into Angular, frontend architecture, and the tools I use every day.

items.title: Building Design Systems That Actually Scale
items.excerpt: After building 3 design systems from scratch, here's what I wish someone had told me earlier.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
Design systems are sold as the holy grail of consistency — but most quietly die within 18 months.

The mistake everyone makes

The instinct is to open your editor and start building. But the real work happens before you write a line.

A design system is not a component library. It is a shared language.

items.title: Angular Signals in 2026 — Honest Take
items.excerpt: Signals became stable in Angular 17. After a year in production, here's my unfiltered opinion.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
When Angular announced Signals, the community was cautiously excited.

Signals did not make our app measurably faster. They made our code easier to reason about.

items.title: NgRx in Production — Lessons After 2 Years
items.excerpt: NgRx is powerful but carries real complexity cost. Here's what we got right and what we'd do differently.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
We adopted NgRx early at Purple Mavens. Two years in, here's the honest review.

NgRx shines at scale. For a small app, the boilerplate will slow you down without meaningful benefit.

items.title: Building a Component Library from Scratch
items.excerpt: How we built 30+ reusable components that cut development time by 60% and what we learned.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
A component library is one of the highest-leverage investments a frontend team can make.

The first deploy with a shared component felt almost anticlimactic. A button rendered. That was the point.

items.title: The Code Review Culture That Made Our Team Better
items.excerpt: Not rules, not checklists — principles that transformed how we give and receive feedback.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
Code review is one of the highest-leverage activities in software engineering.

The goal of a code review is not to find mistakes. It is to ensure the code does what it needs to do.

items.title: 3 Years as a Developer — What I Actually Learned
items.excerpt: The lessons that textbooks and bootcamps will not teach you.
items.author: Naseer
items.body:
Three years ago I wrote my first production line of Angular code at Purple Mavens.

Your code communicates with machines. You communicate with people. Both matter.
